records.title: A Martin kernel with isolated Harnack contact in an annulus
records.description:
For the annulus 1 < |z| < e, with base point a = exp(1/2), the normalized minimal Martin kernel at the inner-boundary point -1 is strictly below the envelope of normalized positive harmonic functions throughout a punctured neighborhood of a. Four explicit positive harmonic competitors yield a uniform first-order gap in every direction. Direct Green-kernel construction and harmonic reflection establish the Martin limit and minimality.

This gives a negative answer to the equality-along-a-Green-line extension in Hayman and Lingham, Research Problems in Function Theory, arXiv:1809.07200v2, Problem 7.42, attributed to Arsove and Johnson. The statement concerns equality along a line issuing from the base point; it does not exclude isolated contact farther away. A dated, bounded priority audit accompanies the authored verification package. An addendum proves that a simpler punctured-disc counterexample is an elementary deduction from classical positive-harmonic representations, including Kohn (1966); this does not establish prior recognition of the Green-line consequence or yield the smooth-annulus theorem. No claim of first historical resolution or certification of current worldwide openness is made.

The deposit contains a concise research note and authored proof source, independent adversarial reviews and reproducibility materials. OpenAI tools were used extensively in solving, drafting and verifying the result. This is an unrefereed preprint, with no completed human peer review or formal proof-assistant certification claimed. Integrity checks and numerical checks do not replace the analytic proof.

records.title: Nonmonotone Argument and Radial Angle of a Support Slit
records.description:
Every global maximizer of the real part of a2+i*10^-24(a4-3a3) in the normalized schlicht class omits a slit with nonmonotone continuous argument and nonmonotone signed and ordinary unsigned radial angles. This gives negative answers to the two questions recorded as Hayman-Lingham Problem 6.72. Compactness provides genuine extremizers, the area theorem bounds the actual slit tip, and a controlled Schiffer natural coordinate identifies a subarc of the actual omitted slit. No explicit maximizing function or uniqueness is required.

The research note credits classical support-slit geometry, Schiffer methods and the Friedland-Schiffer coefficient/control framework. The accompanying package contains manuscript source, immutable authored input, independent analytic and quantitative derivations, exact rational and directed interval checks, and a bounded primary-source priority audit. Complete comparisons include Zemyan (2003, 2005, 2007), Duren-Leung-Schiffer (1983), Zhang-Ma (1991), Brickman (1984), and Goh (1992, 1994). The later Duren commentary (2013 online/2014 print) and Hibschweiler (1995) could not be inspected. Priority therefore cannot be fully cleared. These limitations and other uninspected leads are disclosed; no historical-first priority or continued open status in 2026 is asserted. Finite controls supplement the uniform analytic proofs and are not formal certification of the classical inputs.

AI tools were used extensively in development, writing, reproduction and adversarial verification. This is an unrefereed preprint with internal AI adversarial reviews; it has not received human peer review.

records.title: A qualitative pre-Schwarzian improvement for real schlicht functions
records.description: For normalized univalent functions with real Taylor coefficients, the classical centered pre-Schwarzian disk can be strictly shrunk at every fixed nonreal point, uniformly over the class. Its radius remains sharp on the real diameter. This research note gives a qualitative answer to Hayman–Lingham Problem 6.86 using classical second-coefficient equality, reflection symmetry of the equality domains, and compactness. The gap is uniform on compact nonreal sets. Real disk automorphisms reduce the unknown sharp radius to one variable, and exact examples give lower bounds and two limiting obstructions to a global positive gap. No explicit upper-gap formula, sharp numerical radius, general extremizer or full variability region is determined. No new general method, historical firstness, exhaustive novelty clearance or current-openness guarantee is claimed. The bounded priority audit retains unresolved original-source limits for Jenkins (1960) and Aleksandrov–Popova (1973). Related earlier linear extreme-point and argument estimates are distinguished from the nonlinear derivative quotient. The verification archive preserves the original candidate and controlling scope note, independent analytic/source and priority audits, exact algebraic controls, and explicitly uncertified numerical replays; full third-party source scans are excluded. records.title: Infinite modulus between a compact real set and its real complement
records.description:
For every compact E contained in [0,1], let F be its complement within the real line and let S2 be the circle of radius 2. We prove that positive planar 2-modulus of all curves joining E to S2 forces infinite2-modulus of all curves joining E to F. This answers the explicit implication in the 2018 version of Hayman-Lingham Problem 7.58, including compact sets of zero length and positive capacity. The proof constructs actual boundary values from a pointwise weighted metric, uses critical trace rigidity to force zero length under finite target energy, and then derives a contradiction by small circular connectors. Both global rectifiability and the stated local-off-endpoints convention are treated.

Classical foundations and independently checked audit-composed deductions from older general theory are acknowledged. No claim of firstness, a new mechanism, an earlier explicitly printed resolution, or current worldwide openness is made. Priority searches are bounded; full 2019 wording and an 1982 talk body remain unauthenticated. The deposit contains the preprint and a portable TeX-source, written-proof, independent-reconstruction, integrity-verification and priority-audit archive. records.title: A fixed-area exceptional set for positive squared-pole sums
records.description:
A full affirmative mathematical deduction for Baernstein's question, Hayman–Lingham Problem 7.37 (2307037 / AMR-022-7037). For every finite sum g(z)=sum lambda_j/(z-z_j)^2 with positive weights summing to one and arbitrary, possibly repeated, complex poles, there is one compact exceptional set S(g) of exact planar area pi, independent of R, such that the ordinary finite integral over D_R outside S(g) is at most 2 pi log R + pi(log 2 + 1/e) for every real R greater than one. The leading coefficient 2 pi is sharp; no optimality is claimed for the additive constant.

The deduction combines the established Eremenko–Hamilton 1995 indicator-transform inequality and the Levine–Peres 2009 quadrature/smash-sum construction, with their earlier Astala, Sakai and partial-balayage antecedents credited. No new singular-integral theorem, quadrature construction or general balayage/operator mechanism is claimed. Related recent work by Yongxi Lin and André Guerra is credited. The ingredients were logically available by 2009; a new target-specific application is distinguished from an earlier recorded full solution.

The extensive bounded priority audit identified no verified pre-PR full-target answer but does not certify historical novelty, worldwide first discovery/publication or global openness. Leung preliminary reports titled On a fixed area problem were located in AMS Abstracts 11 (1990), p.181, and 13 (1992), p.440; their mathematical text was inaccessible and relevance remains unresolved. Other unavailable full/final bodies and exact inspection limits are documented. Git version dates do not certify historical public visibility or causal independence.

The source archive preserves twelve original PR artifacts, three distinct mathematical audits, three priority approaches, an independent check that the 2002 EH correction does not affect the imported indicator bound, and the focused Leung supplement. Three standard-library mathematical control programs run offline in ordinary and optimized modes with complete-output comparison and actual failure guards where supplied. A fourth independent target control is reproducible with an explicitly requested, hash-pinned primary-source download. Floating calculations are diagnostics, not validated numerical or formal proof certificates. The universal proof is contained in the note.

records.title: Explicit Beurling-transform counterexamples in an analytic annihilator
records.description:
Both endpoint questions in the bilinear analytic annihilator of Hayman and Lingham, Problem 7.72, have negative answers under the printed negative-kernel convention. The norm-one input v(z)=z/bar(z) on the unit disc annihilates every integrable analytic test function, while its Beurling transform is 1+log|z|^2 and is essentially unbounded. Explicit polynomials v_m(z)=z^2 sum_{j=0}^{m-1}(1-|z|^2)^j lie in the same annihilator, have norm one and have transform norm H_m, the m-th harmonic number. Each fixed polynomial has bounded transform, but no common uniform constant exists.

This is an exposition and independent explicit verification of consequences of classical formulas, with a self-contained proof. Iwaniec published the exact nonpolynomial witness, output and primitive in 1986. Gill published the general positive-angular transform formula in 2010; the polynomial formula and harmonic-number norm follow by elementary specialization. The 2019 Hayman-Lingham book attributes resolution of Problem 7.72 to Volberg. Its cited reference 52 is the 2008 Banuelos-Janakiraman finite-p paper; the current audit did not locate an explicit full-target account there or a separate Volberg proof. This limitation does not refute the book attribution. No new solution, witness, transform mechanism, first polynomial construction, first harmonic-number calculation or current worldwide openness is claimed. Priority for an earlier explicit combined statement in the exact annihilator notation remains unestablished.

The supporting archive preserves the six original submitted files and explicit authored mathematical and priority reviews, source-reading receipts, manuscript source and finite verification programs. The main argument treats all analytic area-L1 tests, principal values almost everywhere, weak derivatives at the origin and boundary, and essential rather than pointwise supremum norms. Root exact coefficient checks, an independent polynomial adversary and a distinct weak-PDE adversary are replayed in normal and both optimized Python modes. A fresh reconstruction begun without candidate history also recovered the witnesses; its optional numerical quadratures are empirical checks, not certified error bounds or automatically replayed exact results. An earlier purported blind family inherited candidate history; it is retained with an explicit exposure correction and is not counted as blind.
